mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 2% for two consecutive months reduces the present value of expected corporate cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 2.0% and remains above for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during the 30-day pre-increase period (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which boosts investor confidence and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by > 10% in a month while UNRATE decreases by > 0.2 percentage points
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns under such conditions are not significantly higher than during neutral labor market periods (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in personal consumption expenditures (CPIAUCSL) exceeding 0.5% for three consecutive months indicates accelerating demand growth, which elevates equity valuations and produces positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: Over 60 such months, the 20-day forward return is not higher than the average of non-expansion months (median test).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) accompanied by a decline in consumer confidence proxies (not available in evidence - so cannot use HOUST here) would imply supply-side weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO decreases by > 2% in a month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns during such episodes are not statistically lower than during the prior 10 contraction months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of FEDFUNDS falls below 1.5%, it signals a shift to accommodative policy, which typically precedes a 20-day S&P 500 advance if the yield curve steepens.
failure_condition: Yield curve steepness (not directly observable but implied) does not correlate with positive 20-day returns (Pearson p > 0.2).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in job openings (not directly observable in the provided proxies) combined with rising pay growth (PAYEMS) would typically drive optimism, but since we cannot proxy job openings, this sketch is omitted and replaced by a regime-based labor signal.
failure_condition: 20-day returns during PAYEMS acceleration are not higher than during flat pay growth (median test).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising retail sales momentum (CPIAUCSL) exceeding 0.3% each, without a corresponding rise in inflation (CPIAUCSL inflation not directly observable but assumed stable), suggests healthy demand that supports positive 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: 60-day returns during such demand phases are not higher than during neutral periods (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a supply shock (evidenced by a one-time INDPRO drop of > 5% followed by persistent weakness), S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days tend to be negative as market adjusts to lower production capacity.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO decreases by > 5% in a single month and remains below prior month's value for 2 months
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns during such episodes are not statistically lower than during stable supply conditions (t-test p > 0.05).
